question: Does the p65 3.100.043 firmware expose the NSH mw/exec primitives and allow executing a RAM stub from an unassigned gap?
prototype_hypothesis: The Band-11-style cave loader can run on p65: write a PIC stub into unassigned RAM with NSH mw and enter it with NSH exec.
callsite_evidence: Mirage device d6e1abd6 (REDMI Watch 6, profile p65) boots the complete 3.100.043 package; the injected NSH lists mw and exec among its builtins.
mw wrote four words at 0x2019e800 (movs r0,#0x5a; ldr r1,[pc,#8]; str r0,[r1]; bx lr; literal 0x2019e820) inside the gap between RAM8_BSS (ends 0x2019e720) and MSP_STACK (starts 0x2019f3e0).
exec 0x2019e801 ran the stub and 0x2019e820 became 0x0000005a, so the default map executes unassigned SRAM and the exec handler accepts an address.
control_flow_evidence: The firmware version property blob is at 0xc3bf9ec; '3.100.043' starts at 0xc3bf9fd (the existing firmware_version_string record is correct).
The build string 'd516af0:nx_best1502p_ap' is at 0x0cbff458 (XIP boot info), not at the existing firmware_build_string record 0xc3bfa25, which points into the charger parameter blob.
ownership_analysis: No ownership claimed for the cave yet; 0x2019e800 is inside a static gap in the IDB and its runtime owner is unproven.
unsafe_assumptions: Emulator evidence only; the p65 has a historical 2026-09 deployment boot-loop (ADR-CAN-007) and has never been deployed by this pack.
The IDB's RAM8_BSS end and MSP_STACK start are taken from the static segments, not from runtime heap ownership.
The watchface Lua engine's os.execute path has not been tested on p65.
recommended_probe: Stage the PIC stage1/stage2 chain in the cave, then verify the Supervisor register path on a Mirage p65 device before any physical attempt.
